### TAG-213: Runtime/parser: bare-name bundle aliasing at invocation boundaries

**Status:** ⬜ Not started

## Software Notes

Depends on [TAG-212](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-212/runtime-execute-statementinvoke-cross-definition-invocation-scalar) (scalar `.invoke` execution) landing first.

[TAG-211](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-211/example-1218-bundling-digits-into-numbers)'s `4BITADD` example uses a compact bare name at a definition's entry/invocation boundary (`4BITADD($A $B $CARRYIN)`) to stand in for a bundle the definition's own header expands (`[A0<> A1<> A2<> A3<>]`). A follow-up diagnostic (parsing `FOOBAR($T)(U<>)` / `BAR($U)(...)`, with each callee's own header declaring the corresponding argument as a bundle) confirmed this **parses**, but the resulting AST gives no indication that it's semantically meaningful:

```
invoke.destinations (1):
  kind=place name='U' text='U<>'   // ordinary scalar Arg — no bundle info attached
```

The fact that `U` corresponds to 3 wires exists only inside the callee's separate definition, not at the call site. So this is unimplemented semantics, not just an unimplemented runtime feature — there's no existing "named bundle" concept in the AST to hang it on (every bundle-kind `Arg` seen so far has an empty `.name` field; only its members are named).

**Scope**

1. **Design question to resolve first, against Fant's** [TAG-211](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-211/example-1218-bundling-digits-into-numbers)  **text** (not by inventing a convention): when a caller-side bare name aliases a callee's declared bundle destination, and that callee is invoked multiple times within one definition (e.g. `FULLADD` called 4 times in `4BITADD`), how are the internal bundle-member names (`K1`/`K2`/`K3`-equivalents) scoped so they don't collide across invocations? Check whether the book specifies a naming/scoping convention before designing one.
2. **Binder logic**, once the naming question is settled:
   * When an invocation's destination or source Arg is a bare scalar-looking place, but the callee's corresponding declared port is a bundle group, expand the bare name into N caller-local places (one per bundle member), scoped to avoid collision with other invocations of the same callee.
   * Record that binding so a later reuse of the same bare name (e.g. as another invocation's source, as in `BAR($U)(...)` consuming what `FOOBAR(...)(U<>)` produced) re-expands consistently and checks arity agreement between the two callees' declared shapes.
3. Extend `.tb.vec` runtime testing to cover a bundled multi-invoke case once the above lands (e.g. `4BITADD` itself, or `FOOBAR`/`BAR`/`PIPE` from the diagnostic).

**Acceptance criteria**

* `4BITADD` (colon removed, per [TAG-211](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-211/example-1218-bundling-digits-into-numbers) diagnosis) resolves correctly end-to-end through `Testbench` for a representative set of 4-bit input pairs.
* The `FOOBAR`/`BAR`/`PIPE` bare-name-aliasing diagnostic resolves correctly, not just parses.
* Naming/scoping behavior for repeated invocations of the same callee is documented (in code comments and/or the Developer's Guide), citing the relevant book section if it specifies one.

Given what's actually blocking right now, I'd split Ticket 2 into two slices — and I think slice 2a alone unblocks `bus`/TAG-180 without needing to resolve the harder open question at all.

## Slice 2a: explicit-bracket group arguments (no open design questions)

This covers exactly what `bus` needs: `fanin($selector_in {$Q1 $Q2 $Q3 $Q4})(...)` and `fanout($selector_out $serialmid)({out1<> out2<> out3<> out4<>})`. The caller explicitly writes out every member, so there's no aliasing, no synthesized names, no collision risk — it's pure positional expansion. This is the case the [TAG-211](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-211/example-1218-bundling-digits-into-numbers) diagnostics (step 1b) already confirmed parses correctly; it just isn't executed or emitted yet.

**Runtime (**`rules.zig`). `scalarPlace` currently rejects any `.group` argument outright. Replace the single-place binding with one that, for a group argument, expects the callee's corresponding declared port to *also* be a group, checks the member counts match, and binds each member positionally:

```
fn bindArgument(allocator: std.mem.Allocator, bindings: *std.ArrayListUnmanaged(Binding), formal: network.Arg, actual: network.Arg) !void {
    if (formal.kind == .group or actual.kind == .group) {
        const formal_group = formal.group orelse return error.InvocationArityMismatch;
        const actual_group = actual.group orelse return error.InvocationArityMismatch;
        if (formal_group.places.len != actual_group.places.len) return error.InvocationArityMismatch;
        for (formal_group.places, actual_group.places) |fp, ap| {
            try bindings.append(allocator, .{ .callee = try scalarPlace(fp), .caller = try scalarPlace(ap) });
        }
        return;
    }
    try bindings.append(allocator, .{ .callee = try scalarPlace(formal), .caller = try scalarPlace(actual) });
}
```

Then in `inlineInvocation`, replace the two `for (inv.sources, callee.sources) |actual, formal| try bindings.append(...)` loops with calls to `bindArgument`. Everything downstream (renaming, `checkInvocable`) is unchanged, since it just walks the flat `bindings` list either way. `mutex` vs `bundle` vs `arbitration` doesn't matter for this binding step — it's always "N named members, matched by position to the callee's own group-shaped port." The mutex-specific "only one member is actually valid at a time" behavior isn't something the binder needs to enforce; it's just a property of how `bus` happens to drive `Q1`–`Q4` in practice.

**Emitter (**`invocation.zig`). `writeInvocationArgument`'s `.group` branch currently just writes one `null_value`. It needs to expand into one signal *per member*, each wired to that member's real value — mirroring what `bindArgument` does on the runtime side:

```
if (argument.kind == .group) {
    if (argument.group) |group| {
        for (group.places, 0..) |member, member_index| {
            const member_signal = try std.fmt.allocPrint(allocator, "invocation_{d}_arg_{d}_{d}", .{ invocation_index, argument_index, member_index });
            defer allocator.free(member_signal);
            const id = try placeName(allocator, member);
            defer allocator.free(id);
            try writer.print("  {s} <= {s};\n", .{ member_signal, id });
        }
    }
    return;
}
```

`writeInvocationSignals` (which declares the `invocation_N_arg_M` signals) and `writeInvocationInstance`'s port-map loop both need the matching change: when `inv.sources[argument_index]` is a group, declare/connect N signals (`invocation_N_arg_M_0` … `_3`) against the callee's N real port names, instead of one. Destinations need the same treatment for `{out1<> out2<> out3<> out4<>}` — each output member gets its own signal, wired to its own formal port, rather than the current single `invocation_N_output_M <= null_value` plus one mapped connection.

**Acceptance for 2a:** `bus`'s corrected definition passes all 20 rows through `.tb.vec`, and its GHDL emission analyzes cleanly (once the workdir isolation fix from last time is also in place, so `AND`/`OR`/`NOT`-style name reuse across examples doesn't independently break things).

## Slice 2b: bare-name aliasing (needs the book check first)

This is `4BITADD($A $B $CARRYIN)` and the `FOOBAR`/`BAR`/`PIPE` diagnostic — a bare scalar-looking name standing in for an entire group, with no brackets at the call site, resolved purely by matching against the callee's declared shape. This is where the real open question lives: how repeated invocations of the same callee (four `FULLADD` calls in `4BITADD`) avoid their internal bundle-member names colliding.
